title: agent-collective: /collective TUI and Tern block
subtitle: A keyboard panel for seeing the sessions in your profile and messaging them, inside omp/pi and as a native Tern block.
tldr: Five desktop screens. In omp: `/collective` as a full-screen overlay (session list, a thread with one peer, rename) plus a bottom-panel variant. In Tern: the same data as a plugin block beside your agent panes. Pick the theme, the omp layout, message logging, offline rows and how Tern sends.

sections.title: Brief
sections.lead: One panel answers "who is in this profile, what are they doing, and what did we say" without spending a model turn.

items.md: One running omp or pi agent with the extension loaded; it has a callsign such as `be-audio-001`.
Every session in one omp profile (`~/.agent-collective/<profile>/`). The TUI never shows another profile.
A session this one has messaged or heard from; starred and listed first.
A callsign still reserved for a session that is not running (up to 7 days after it last ran).
The messages this session exchanged with one peer, oldest first.

blocks.md:
**Who:** you, running 5–30 sessions across worktrees, up to 3 per directory. **Where:** inside an omp or pi terminal (`/collective` opens it with `ctx.ui.custom`, both hosts support it), or as a Tern pane when the sessions run in Tern.

Each screen must let you:

- **Sessions:** see every session in the profile with its state (working, idle, quiet, offline), directory and harness. Also where it runs (Tern pane, herdr pane or tty); filter by text; star contacts first.
- **Thread:** read what this session and one peer said, with each delivery's outcome (woken, aside, coalesced, refused) and hop; write a message and send it.
- **Tern block:** the same list as a native Tern block, plus *go to pane*, because Tern knows where each session's pane is.

All data comes from files the extension already writes: records (`<pid>.json`), claims (`names/`) and session state (`sessions/<id>.json`). Reading them costs no model turn and no socket traffic. Two things are new and need your pick: a per-session message log (the thread view needs it) and a way for Tern to send.

items.text: Which framework do the screens use?
items.sub: Recommend Plain kit: these are terminal cells, so only colour tokens and a monospace grid matter.
items.detail: The real UI is drawn by omp's TUI (`Component.render(width) → string[]`) and by Tern's TSP nodes (`tern.ui.table`, `list`, `badge`), not by HTML. The mock only needs a character grid and the theme's colours; a component framework would mislead about what can be drawn.

items.sub: Recommend omp dark: it is what the overlay sits on; Tern re-skins its block with its own theme anyway.

items.text: Choose how /collective opens in omp and pi
items.sub: Recommend full-screen overlay: 25 sessions need the rows; Esc returns to the transcript.
items.detail: Full-screen: the **Sessions** and **Thread** screens. Bottom panel: the **Sessions, bottom panel** variant; the transcript stays visible above, 8 sessions fit before scrolling, and the thread opens full-screen anyway.

items.text: Decide whether each session keeps a message log
items.sub: Recommend log: the thread view and outcome history need it; cost is one small file append per message.
items.detail: **Keep a log:** append one JSON line per sent or received message to `sessions/<session-id>.log.jsonl` (time, peer, direction, hop, outcome, body), capped at the last 500 lines. **No log:** the Thread screen can show only messages that arrived since the TUI opened; outcomes of earlier sends are lost.

items.text: Decide whether offline callsigns appear in the list
items.sub: Recommend show, dimmed: a send to them is answered "offline" anyway, so seeing them avoids the surprise.

items.text: Choose how the Tern block sends a message
items.sub: Recommend a CLI in the package: Tern plugins can run processes but cannot open unix sockets.
items.detail: Tern's Luau API has `tern.fs` (read records) and `tern.process.run`, but no socket client. **CLI:** ship `bin/agent-collective send <callsign> <message>` in the package; the block runs it, and the peer sees the message as from `you (via Tern)` at hop 0. **Go to pane only:** the block lists sessions and jumps to their pane; you type there.

sections.title: Screens
sections.lead: Five screens on desktop: four in omp/pi, one Tern block; wireframes with real labels and data shaped like today's stanbam profile.
